question: How accurate does the predictor have to be before taking one box has a higher expected value than taking both, and why does that not settle what to do?
finding: With a million in the opaque box and a thousand in the clear one, one-boxing has the higher evidential expected value once the predictor is right more than 50.05% of the time, yet in every one of 100,000 simulated plays taking both boxes would have paid exactly $1,000 more.
limit: Both calculations are correct arithmetic, so the page cannot say which is the rational choice: the disagreement is over which probabilities belong in the sum.
